item.title: C Permit in Basel-Landschaft: Requirements and Application
item.description: In the Canton of Basel-Landschaft: 10 years of residence, 5 for EU/EFTA, integration, language, and procedure for the C permit.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - C: normally 10 years of residence - EU/EFTA: 5 years of residence - Integration and language enter the evaluation - SEM: reference for foreign permits
## Key Facts - Permit C → domicile - Ordinary rule → 10 years of residence - EU/EFTA citizens → 5 years of residence - Ordinary naturalization → C + 10 year permit - Years between 8 and 18 → count double - Naturalization → cantonal and communal requirements
Ten years of residence is the standard rule for obtaining a C residence permit in Switzerland. For EU and EFTA citizens, the threshold is five years. These are the two numbers that should be put at the heart of the check for those who live in the canton of Basel-Landschaft and are planning to switch from a residence permit to a right of residence.
C is not a simple extension of the B permit. In the classification of foreign permits, the L permit refers to short-term residence of up to one year, B to renewable residence, C to domicile and G to the condition of cross-border commuter. The institutional reference indicated for this framework is the SEM. Distinguishing the categories avoids using the duration of B or the situation of G as if they were already a C permit.
### The rule of years of residence
The statement is not the only element called up by the source. The Basel-Landschaft corner also includes integration criteria and language skills. These are elements to be checked alongside the length of residence, without replacing them with a simple sum of the years. The application, therefore, should not be based only on the date of arrival, but on the combination of duration, integration and language provided for by the applicable framework.
The expression early release indicates a case history distinct from the ordinary rule. The reference material does not replace the ordinary threshold with a different number of years; for this reason, the application must separate the verification of the possible advance from the standard calculation and the integration and language criteria.
The same title also plays a role in ordinary naturalization. For that path, you need a C permit and ten years of residence; the years between eight and eighteen count double, while the cantonal and municipal requirements remain to be considered. Domicile and naturalization are not synonymous: the former is the residence permit, the latter is a procedure with additional conditions.
For those who organize the stay in Switzerland, the administrative requirement can be accompanied by a comparison on the costo della vita in Svizzera, without confusing the personal balance with the verification of the permit. The question point remains the C in the Canton of Basel-Landschaft, with the correct threshold and the criteria indicated. ## How to read the right threshold
For concrete planning, the first difference is the citizenship relevant to the count. The same question about the C permit does not read the same for everyone: the rule indicated is ten years, while for the EU/EFTA it is five. Before estimating the time of the application, it is therefore necessary to place the case in the correct category; using the wrong threshold shifts the entire planning.
### Three paths that should not overlap
| Verification | Source data | Practical use | |---|---|---| | Ordinary Rule C | 10 years of residence | Basis of counting | | EU/EFTA citizens | 5 years of residence | Threshold indicated for this group | | Ordinary naturalization | C + 10 years | Separate path |
The second step concerns the quality of the course. Integration and language skills are not a decorative addition: they are part of the criteria mentioned for the C permit in the canton of Basel-Landschaft. The person preparing the application should therefore read the time requirement together with these two profiles, instead of considering reaching the age as an automatic answer.
The third step is not to confuse C and naturalization. The years between eight and eighteen count twice as much for ordinary naturalization. This element belongs to that path, which already requires the C permit, ten years and cantonal and municipal requirements; it should not be automatically transferred to the calculation of domicile.
The issue of early release also requires precision. It is a case distinct from the general rule: the application should not jump directly from the declared duration to the outcome, without separating the time threshold, qualitative criteria and possible exception. The most solid reading is to formulate three checks: which threshold applies, which aspects of integration and language must be examined and whether we are talking about the ordinary procedure or an early release.
The territorial reference remains the Canton of Basel-Landschaft, while the reference for the foreign permit framework is the SEM. For other aspects of resident life, a separate tool, such as the LAMal e cassa malati comparison, can be used without attributing an effect to that topic on the requirements of the C.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## Checklist before the request
### The Control Sequence
An application review procedure in the canton of Basel-Landschaft can be organized in five steps. The sequence is used to read the requirements in order.
1. Identify the current title. Start from the actual category: L, B, C or G. L concerns the short term up to one year, B the renewable residence, C the domicile, G the cross-border commuter. This step prevents confusing the application for domicile with the simple renewal of another title.
2. Classify the residence regime. Check whether the case falls within the EU/EFTA. The threshold to be used is five years for this group and, as a rule of thumb, ten years in the other cases listed in the general framework.
3. Reconstruct the count. Use residence as the main variable and do not move the double years mechanism into the calculation of C: the count of years between 8 and 18 is indicated for ordinary naturalization.
4. Complement the qualitative criteria. The assessment includes integration and language skills. If early release is envisaged, treat it as a separate assessment from the ordinary threshold; do not automatically replace the calculation of five or ten years with an assumption.
5. If the next goal is to naturalize, check the combination requested: C permit, ten years of residence, double counting of years between eight and eighteen, and cantonal and municipal requirements. This is an additional path, not an automatic consequence of applying for C.
The institutional reference indicated for foreign permits is the SEM. For an application placed in Basel-Landschaft, this sequence allows you to keep a distinction between title, years, integration, language and any early issue. It avoids two opposite mistakes: stopping at the number of years alone or giving the early issue an automatic effect.

For those living in Switzerland, the guide to KVG health insurance premiums in the canton of Vaud starts with a precise rule: health insurance is mandatory for residents and must be taken out within three months of arrival. For those who arrive in the country during the year, the indicated deadline remains three months from arrival: the comparison begins with the insurance position and the applicable territory, not with a single national tariff.
This distinction also applies to the reading of the offers: geographical reference and year must be consistent, otherwise the comparison between premiums loses value. The 2026 guide is used to sort these items before choosing.
The KVG/KVG system is a private insurance with per capita premiums. It is not a tax and it is not a salary contribution. It should therefore be distinguished in the balance sheet from AHV/AHV and BVG/BVG social security contributions, as well as direct federal tax and VAT. The comparison with the payslip or the costo della vita in Svizzera is clearer when these items remain separate.

The premiums are linked to the canton and region. For the canton of Vaud, the figure to be used in 2026 must therefore refer to the applicable territory; a national average or the value of another canton does not replace that reference. The average KVG premiums are figures indexed each year: the value useful for the balance sheet is the one updated for the year and area considered.

Then there is the reduction in premiums, referred to as the cantonal subsidy. In the case of the canton of Vaud, the verification must be maintained at the cantonal level, together with the premium linked to the region. In this way, the 2026 guide separates three data that are often mixed: insurance obligation, per capita cost and cantonal support. When moving from one insurance fund to another, indicating the deductible avoids comparing offers built on different conditions. The choice remains legible only if the threshold is shown next to the premium and the territory, instead of being left implicit.
The third level is the subsidy. The premium reduction is cantonal and should not be treated as an identical national item in every territory. In the canton of Vaud, the support must be checked together with the applicable cantonal situation and the premium linked to the region. This is the item that can affect the overall cost of coverage and should be included in the comparison, not added later.
### Separate insurance, taxes and wages
A reliable simulation does not add the KVG to the wage deductions as if it were the same thing. The premium is per capita; AHV/AHV and BVP/BVG belong to social security contributions. Direct federal tax and VAT are also different items. Keeping these categories separate avoids attributing the functioning of a tax or wage levy to the health insurance company and helps to read the cost of living in Switzerland.
For the change of cash insurer, the comparison must use the same three filters: canton or region, adult deductible and cantonal premium reduction. item.description: In the canton of Aargau, the 2026 cost of living should be viewed across three tax levels, LAMal within 3 months, and a national comparison of rents, groceries and transport.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Taxation on three levels: federal, cantonal and municipal. - The KVG must be concluded within 3 months of arrival. - KVG premiums vary by canton and region. - There is no federal minimum wage.
## Key Facts - Taxation → federal IFD + cantonal and municipal taxes - KVG → mandatory for residents - Deductibles for adults → CHF 300/500/1000/1500/2000/2500 - Maximum hours → 45 or 50 hours per week - Minimum holidays → 4 weeks - Maternity → 14 weeks at 80% - L permit → up to 1 year - Security deposit → maximum 3 months' rent
Three tax levels — direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax — are the first element to separate when reading the Swiss cost of living 2026 with a focus on the canton of Aargau. Each canton has its own law and multiplier; in municipalities, the multiplier applies to the cantonal tax. The national comparison is therefore not reduced to a single rate valid throughout Switzerland.
### Who handles which article
The FTA/ESTV manages the IFD and VAT. The cantonal administrations, on the other hand, manage cantonal and municipal taxes. The FSIO/BSV covers social security, including AHV/IV/VVG, and does not set taxes. FSO/BFS produces statistics and does not set rates. For those who compare Aargau with other cantons, this distinction prevents a statistical source from being used as if it were a tax authority.
The budget reading includes four blocks: rents, food shopping, transport and insurance. On the health front, the KVG is mandatory for residents and must be stipulated within three months of arrival. The premium is per capita, not a tax or a salary contribution; it changes according to canton and region, while the premium reduction is a cantonal subsidy. For adults, the deductibles are CHF 300, 500, 1,000, 1,500, 2,000 and 2,500.
For housing, the federal tenancy law is the same in each canton: the security deposit cannot exceed three months' rent and must be in an escrow account in the name of the tenant. The landlord's notice of termination is valid only on the official cantonal form; any dispute must be submitted within 30 days to the conciliation authority. This is a national rule that differs from the level of rents, which must be read here as a separate item.
To transform these elements into a readable comparison, it is advisable to keep daily prices separate from the rules that change between institutional levels. The costo della vita in Svizzera helps to sort the general items; for the health part, the confronto LAMal e cassa malati remains distinct from the salary calculation. Thus, the canton of Aargau enters the national comparison through the tax and insurance structure provided for the cantons. ## How to really read the comparison
The cost of living in the canton of Aargau is not measured by adding up heterogeneous items without looking at who determines them. For a comparison with other cantons, the practical question is twofold: what expenditure weighs on the budget and what rule establishes its amount or form. Rent, food expenditure and transport are issues to be observed; taxation, KVG, contributions and social security require an institutional reading.
### A grid so as not to mix the planes
| Area | Data to be verified | Practical reading | |---|---|---| | Taxation | Federal IFD, cantonal and municipal taxes; Cantonal law and multiplier | Separating the three levels | | KVG/KVG | Premium per capita, canton or region, cantonal premium reduction | Do not treat it as a wage deduction | | Jobs | No federal minimum wage; some cantons have one | Check the territorial rule | | Home | Federal Tenancy Law; Filing for up to three months | Separate initial guarantee and rent |
The most useful contrast is that between an expense linked to the territory and an expense linked to the person. The LAMal premiums follow the canton and the region and are per capita; the premium reduction follows a cantonal channel. Salary deductions, on the other hand, require a distinction to be made between contribution, sector, age group and ceiling. Therefore, a comparison between two budgets cannot stop at the gross salary.
On the labor market, the canton of Aargau must be read within a Swiss rule without a federal minimum wage: some cantons have their own threshold. The maximum hours also depend on the sector: 45 hours a week in industry, offices and sales, 50 in other sectors. The minimum holidays are four weeks, five for those under 20 years of age. These elements affect income and time planning, without automatically turning into a price of rent or groceries.
Discipline is required for the 2026 figures. The third pillar 3a ceiling, the BVG coordination threshold or deduction, the AD/AC ceiling, the average KVG premiums and the median salary are indexed values each year. If the reference year is not the correct one, a precise amount can make the comparison less reliable. The busta paga svizzera helps to separate the deductions; the guida AVS/LPP e rendita is used to read the pension without confusing it with taxes.

To use the comparison on the canton of Aargau in an operational way, the correct sequence starts from the date of arrival and ends with the calculation of disposable income. No invented estimates are needed: the applicable rules are needed and, for indexed figures, the official figure for the year.
### 1. Set the health deadline
If you are a resident, consider the KVG as compulsory insurance and record the deadline of three months from arrival to take it out. The adult deductibles available are CHF 300, 500, 1,000, 1,500, 2,000 and 2,500. The premium remains per capita and varies by canton and region; a premium reduction, when provided, is a cantonal subsidy. The sequence avoids including the KVG among the percentage contributions to the salary.
### 2. Reconstruct the payslip
Separately mark AHV/IV/EO: 5.3% to be paid by the employee and 10.6% overall to the employer. For ALV/HC use 1.1% up to the annual ceiling; for UVG/LAA consider 0.7–1.5% depending on the sector. On the coordinated BVG salary, apply the indicated age range: 7% between 25 and 34 years old, 10% between 35 and 44, 15% between 45 and 54, 18% from 55 years old up to the reference age. Do not add these items to the per capita premium of the KVG.
### 3. Rebuild the tax authorities
Divide the verification into federal IFD, cantonal tax and municipal tax. For IFD and VAT, the institutional reference is FTA/ESTV; for the cantonal and municipal administrations, the cantonal administrations are responsible. FSIO/BSV remains the social security institution, while FSO/BFS provides statistics: neither should be used to allocate tax rates.
### 4. Check the location
In federal tenancy law, the security deposit does not exceed three months' rent and goes to an escrow account in the tenant's name. If the landlord gives notice of termination, check the official cantonal form; the complaint must be brought to the conciliation authority within 30 days.
### 5. Check your calendar and work exit
To plan the relationship, consider a maximum of 45 or 50 hours per week depending on the sector, at least four weeks of vacation, maternity leave of 14 weeks at 80% through EO and paternity leave of two weeks. The notice periods are one month in the first year, two from the second to the ninth, three from the tenth.

item.description: Three arrests, eight searches and five servers seized: the operation against KillSec recovered at least 110 terabytes of stolen data.

## In brief - Three arrests and eight searches in four countries - Recovered at least 110 terabytes of stolen data - Attacks on Swiss companies between October 2023 and June 2025
## Key Facts - Group → KillSec (or KillSecurity) - Operation → dismantling of an IT structure - Arrests → three - Searches → eight - Countries → Spain, Greece, the United Kingdom and Romania - Servers seized → five - Data recovered → at least 110 terabytes - → attacks against several Swiss companies, between October 2023 and June 2025
On Wednesday, a large international operation made it possible to dismantle the IT structure used by the KillSec ransomware group, also known as KillSecurity. The toll includes three arrests, eight searches in Spain, Greece, the United Kingdom and Romania, the seizure of five servers and the recovery of at least 110 terabytes of stolen data.
### The Swiss survey
This was announced by the Federal Office of Police (fedpol) and the Office of the Attorney General of Switzerland (OAG). Since the summer of 2025, the two agencies have been conducting an investigation into a series of attacks against various Swiss companies, which took place between October 2023 and June 2025. The criminal proceedings concern data theft, abusive access to a computer system, data damage and extortion.
### How ransomware works
The mechanism described in the source follows a precise sequence. The perpetrators improperly enter the victim's computer system, copy and extract the data of interest, then encrypt the servers. Only then do they demand a ransom in exchange for the decryption key; the request is often made in cryptocurrency.
### Double extortion
KillSec practices the so-called double extortion. After the encryption of the servers, if the company refuses to pay, the authors threaten to publish the data on the darknet. The refusal may depend, for example, on a backup made before the theft: the restoration of the data does not eliminate, according to the dynamics described, the threat of dissemination of the information already copied.
Fedpol and the OAG participated in the investigations coordinated by Europol and Eurojust together with seven other countries. The communication released on Thursday underlines the need for cooperation between national and international partners: "Given the international nature of cybercrime, close cooperation between the different partners, both nationally and internationally, is essential," reads a statement released on Thursday. ## The risk does not end with encryption
For a Swiss company, the sequence described separates two problems. Server encryption is about access to systems; copying and extraction happen first and feed the threat of publication. The backup cited by the source can therefore explain the ransom refusal, but it does not automatically delete the second lever used by the group. It is the difference between recovering one's own systems and preventing the data already stolen from being disseminated.
| Step | What the source indicates | Pressure on the victim | |---|---|---| | Access | Unauthorized entry into the computer system | The attack starts | | Extraction | Copying data of interest | Data is stolen | | Encryption | Encrypted servers | Decryption key is asked | | Backup | Can Motivate Ransom Rejection | Darknet Threat Remains | | Payment | Ransom is often demanded in cryptocurrency | The demand takes an economic form |
### A balance sheet to be read without overinterpretation
The reference to at least 110 terabytes refers to the material recovered in the operation. The source does not attribute that volume to a single Swiss company, does not indicate the identity of the companies involved and does not report any payments. Sticking to this data avoids turning the balance sheet of the operation into an estimate of the damage for each victim.
The geography should also be read without simplification. The investigation stems from attacks against Swiss companies, while the operation involved four countries and involved the seizure of servers. The participation of fedpol and the OAG, together with Europol, Eurojust and seven other countries, shows a chain of investigation spread beyond Swiss territory alone.
The text does not indicate the sectors involved. The reference therefore remains limited to several Swiss companies; those looking for a distinct picture of the productive fabric can consult the aziende che assumono.

1. **Separate dates.** The attacks indicated in the investigation date back to the period between October 2023 and June 2025. The Swiss investigation has been conducted since the summer of 2025. The dismantling operation took place on Wednesday, while the communication was released on Thursday.

The trade association Physioswiss has collected 112,000 signatures throughout Switzerland in support of higher fees for physiotherapy. Twenty-six cantonal petitions will now be submitted to the competent authorities in the course of October, the association said in a statement. Deliveries have already taken place in Neuchâtel and Zug.
### The central request: plus 30 percent Specifically, the association is calling for a fee increase of at least 30 percent. According to Physioswiss, this would allow practices to cover operating costs and pay fair salaries. A prerequisite, the statement highlights, to ensure access to physiotherapy care for all patients in the vicinity of their home. "Now the cantons are called upon to take the economic reality of physiotherapy practices seriously and to set fair rates," says director Osman Bešić, quoted in the note.
### Antecedents: the 2023-2024 conflict As early as 2023, the industry had drawn attention to its financial situation. At that time, Physioswiss had collected 283,000 signatures against a tariff intervention planned by the Federal Council, which was then implemented in spring 2024. This triggered an internal conflict that led to the creation of a new association called Prophysio. A new tariff model, which is expected to come into force in 2027, proposes a switch to performance-based pricing with a time component: physiotherapy services will be billed at five-minute intervals. The current petitions, on the other hand, concern the setting of cantonal tariff point values. ### Impact on patients and the healthcare system The requested tariff increase of 30% would have a direct impact on the KVG/KVG system. Physiotherapy services are reimbursed by compulsory health insurance on medical prescription. An adjustment of the cantonal tariffs of the tariff point would result in higher costs for health insurers, which could be reflected in the 2026 premiums. The cantons, which are responsible for setting the point values, will have to balance the sustainability of the studies with the burden on the winners.
### Comparison with the situation 2023 The current signature collection (112,000 signatures) is lower than in 2023 (283,000), when the opposition was directed against federal intervention. Today, petitions target the cantonal level, where the value of the tariff point is decided. The fragmentation into 26 separate petitions reflects the federal architecture: each canton sets its own point value, creating territorial disparities that physiotherapists have been denouncing for some time.
### The new 2027 model: opportunities and risks The transition to billing at five-minute intervals from 2027 introduces a time component that should better remunerate the complexity of treatments. Physioswiss defends this novelty. However, the transition requires management adjustments in practices and new tariff agreements between trade associations and insurers. Until 2027, the values of the cantonal point remain the main lever for economic sustainability.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ### What happens now: calendar and actors The petitions have been or will be delivered to the cantonal governments and parliaments by October 2024. Each canton will follow its own procedure: in some cases the government can decide directly, in others the approval of the legislature is required. Decision times vary from a few months to over a year. Physiotherapists and patients can monitor the process by contacting the cantonal health department or by consulting the website of the local Grand Council.
### How to orient yourself as a patient Anyone who receives physiotherapy on prescription does not pay the tariff directly: health insurance reimburses less the deductible and the deductible (10%). Checking the coverage of your health insurance company and comparing premiums remains the main tool.

## In brief - FDF-SNB agreement for the financial years 2026-2030 - Annual maximum of six billion to the Confederation and cantons - Base of two billion and four additions of one billion - Minimum provisions from 10% to 8% from 2026
## Key Facts - Signatories → FDF and SNB - Period → financial years 2026-2030 - Maximum distribution → six billion francs per year - Basic amount → two billion francs - Possible additions → four of a billion - Profit thresholds → CHF 10, 20, 30 and CHF 40 billion - Minimum provisions → 10% to 8% from financial year 2026 - Condition → financial situation of the SNB
Up to six billion francs per year can be paid to the Confederation and the cantons for the financial years 2026-2030. The limit depends on the financial situation of the SNB. The new agreement was signed by the Federal Department of Finance (FDF) and the issuing institution, as reported in a statement released on Thursday evening.
### The structure of the maximum amount
The mechanism starts with a basic amount of two billion francs. This amount is paid out when the balance sheet profit amounts to at least two billion. Four distributions, each of one billion, can be added to the basis, activated when the profit reaches 10, 20, 30 or 40 billion francs respectively.
The ceiling of six billion is therefore the sum of the base and the four possible additions. The agreement links the level of possible sums to the achievement of determined profit values. For the Confederation and the cantons, it thus establishes a multi-annual framework linked to the SNB's results.
### Provisions and residual profit
In accordance with the law, the SNB must first build up provisions for operating income. The aim is to maintain the currency reserves at the required level. The equity capital has improved in recent years. For this reason, the minimum allocation to provisions will increase from 10% to 8% from the 2026 financial year, but with annual approval by the Bank Council.
After the provisions, the residual profit is in principle available for distribution. The FDF and the SNB set the reference values in a multi-year agreement to ensure a constant distribution over the medium term. The order indicated is therefore provisions, residual profit and distribution between the Confederation and the cantons. The most concrete consequence of the new agreement is the distinction between the theoretical maximum and the sum that can actually be distributed. Six billion is not a guaranteed amount every year: the basis requires a balance sheet profit of at least two billion, while the other four instalments depend on specific thresholds and the financial situation of the SNB. The level reached must therefore be checked before considering the payment.
### A grid to read thresholds
| Profit achieved | Possible structure | |---|---| | At least 2 billion | Base of 2 billion | | 10 billion | Base plus 1 billion | | 20 billion | Base plus 2 billion | | 30 billion | Base plus 3 billion | | 40 billion | Base plus 4 billion |
The table reflects the scale described by the FDF. Each additional step is subject to the general condition of the SNB's financial situation. The ceiling of six billion can only be reached with the base and all four additional distributions provided for in the agreement.
The second element to be kept separate is the provision. The increase from 10% to 8% concerns the minimum allocation to the strengthening of currency reserves, not a quota already allocated to the Confederation or the cantons. In addition, the annual approval of the Bank Council remains necessary. The 8% does not therefore make it possible to calculate the final amount available on its own.

## In brief - Draghi spoke at ETH Zurich. - He calls for supranational reforms and an EU roadmap. - The debt/GDP ratio will reach 130% by 2040. - AI requires 1,3 trillion by 2030.
## Key facts - Speaker → Mario Draghi - Location → ETH Zurich - Event → anniversary of the SNB lecture series - Debt/GDP → 130% by 2040 - Investments in AI → 1,3 trillion by 2030
In Zurich, at ETH Zurich, Mario Draghi invited the European Union to look to Switzerland's example. The former president of the European Central Bank and former Italian prime minister spoke at the anniversary of the Swiss National Bank's lecture series in honor of economist Karl Brunner. As guest of honor, he brought the scale needed to address growth back to center stage.
The reference is precise: according to Draghi, Switzerland is not a federation but a Confederation in which, in some sectors, real growth objectives can be achieved only on a large scale. The proposal to the EU is therefore supranational. For the former prime minister, Europe must overcome nationalisms and pursue greater integration, comparable to that which unites the United States of America, in order to regain a role in the global geoeconomy.
### Draghi's proposal
> «Supranational reforms have become the most important lever for growth. A detailed plan for implementing these reforms was outlined in the report on Europe's competitiveness, and much of it is contained in the EU roadmap. The first thing we must do is implement this roadmap,» said Draghi, guest of honor at the event.
The speech, more focused on monetary policy than on economic policy compared with other occasions, described a Europe facing a different phase from that of a few years ago. Its economy is the most open in the world, but it must contend with Donald Trump's tariff policy, Chinese aggressiveness, and two conflicts whose end is not in sight.
### Debt, inflation and artificial intelligence
Growth, according to Draghi, is the lever on which Europe can still act, while interest rates respond to global synchronization. Fiscal consolidation therefore depends on economic expansion. Monetary policy remains decisive for controlling inflation, but it cannot solve everything: when debt dynamics worsen, markets put the central bank's commitment to the test and demand to know how it will respond to every scenario.
Draghi indicated a debt/GDP ratio of 130% by 2040 and unavoidable fiscal consolidation in the medium term. Spending cuts and tax increases alone would hardly be enough. On the technological front, rapid AI adoption could add up to 0,4 percentage points to total factor productivity growth over the next decade. To make AI competitive in the EU, 1,3 trillion in investment would be needed by 2030, along with 100 billion from the EU budget to reduce its risk. ## Reading for those who live in Switzerland
For a resident or worker in Switzerland, the news has a precise but limited practical effect: it does not announce a new tax, a wage change or a decision by the SNB. Its weight lies in the way it describes European growth and in the fact that the Swiss reference is used to discuss the ability to act on a large scale. The place of intervention should not be confused with the recipient of the proposal: Draghi spoke in Zurich, but addressed his roadmap to the European Union.

The decisive word is integration. In Draghi's reconstruction, some goals cannot be effectively achieved by isolated states. Switzerland was called into question as a Confederation, not as the recipient of a package of reforms announced on the stage of the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology. For those who follow national economic policy, the distinction prevents turning a discourse on EU growth into an immediate measure for households, businesses or workers in Switzerland.

The operational point, for the reader, is therefore not to attribute to the SNB a position that does not appear in the text.

The first is fiscal: consolidation depends on growth and, according to Draghi, spending cuts and tax increases alone may not produce the necessary results. The second is monetary: the interest rate is increasingly set outside Europe, while growth remains the lever on which Europe can act. The third is technological: the single market and AI are presented as potential sources of growth and productivity, not as already achieved results.

In August 2026, the Swiss consumer price index rose by 0.4% in just one month and by 0.8% year-on-year. In the same month, the prices of petrol, diesel and heating oil also rose. The question raised by the source is concrete: what is really left in the wallet when the statistics speak of low inflation, but daily expenses are increasing?
The point is not just about fuel. Energy enters transport, production, logistics, heating, services and basic necessities. For this reason, the pressure felt by those who pay for a full tank or a bill can also appear in other expenditures: not as a single item, but as a cascading effect on the cost of almost everything that is consumed.
### The tax knot
According to the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security, the tax on mineral oils amounts to 76.82 cents per litre on petrol and 79.57 cents on diesel. VAT is added to these amounts. The source points out that this does not mean that the Confederation collects exactly one franc per litre. However, the figure remains close to that threshold and indicates that a very large part of what is paid at the pump does not go to oil, transport or the distributor, but to the state in the form of taxes.
The revenue confirms the size of the issue: in 2025 the tax on mineral oils alone guaranteed the public coffers 4.367 billion francs. The question posed in the text is therefore fiscal as well as economic: when high energy prices erode purchasing power, why should the state continue to collect in full even on prices that continue to rise? And if families and businesses are under pressure, shouldn't the tax authorities at least temporarily take a step back?
The issue can also be read through the costo della vita in Svizzera, because filling up and heating are part of the expenses that affect every day. The effect on the balance sheet can be seen in the comparison between the average and the individual day. A national statistic can describe a small increase, while those who live in Switzerland face a full tank, the heating bill, the groceries, the renewal of a lease or the cost of a bus or train. The source does not present these items as the same tax: it lines them up to show the distance between an average index and the actual expenditure.
If income does not grow at the same rate, inflation ceases to be an abstract percentage. It becomes a reduction in the space available for other expenditures. The mechanism described is simple: oil increases and pays the consumer; then transport, heating, production and distribution increase, and the consumer pays again. Pressure can then reach the pump directly or indirectly in goods and services.
### Where the price increase is transferred
The sequence can be read as follows:
| Voice indicated in the source | Where it occurs | |---|---| | Petrol & Diesel | Fuel & Transport | | Heating oil | bill and heating | | Energy | Production, Logistics & Distribution | | Goods & Services | Grocery & Daily Necessities |
The transition from one item to another makes it difficult to read the increase by looking at a single expense. Instead, the source invites us to consider the complete chain: from fuel to transport, from heating to services and goods that arrive at the expense.
For a household, the problem is not just how much a single item costs, but how many times energy reappears in the same budget. Fuel is a visible expense; heating is when the bill arrives; the effect on production and logistics can be incorporated into the price of basic necessities. For a company, the same chain affects transport, production and distribution, while households and businesses remain under pressure.
Here lies the difference between the price at the pump and the cost of living: the former is immediate, the latter collects the effects that accumulate. To order the comparison between income and expenses, this analysis can be combined with the guide to busta paga svizzera.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the net salary calculator and the tax return guide. To transform this reading into a check of one's own budget, the path can remain adherent to the items listed in the source. There is no need to add assumptions about consumption or income: just separate what is seen directly from what comes in a cascade effect.
### Four steps to read the financial statements
1. Collect in a single list the expenses that the source puts in the foreground: full tank, heating bill, groceries, renewal of a rental contract, bus or train. The goal is to have the monthly bill in front of you without confusing the official figure with the daily outlay.
2. Then divide the items into two groups. In the first put gasoline, diesel and heating oil, i.e. the energy costs indicated directly. In the second write down the sectors that can receive the cascading effect: transport, production, logistics, services and basic necessities.
3. Put income next to it and ask yourself if it grows at the same rate as expenditures. It is the comparison that transforms inflation from a percentage into purchasing power: if the final bill rises more than income, the difference is felt in the balance sheet.
4. Keep the price paid at the pump separate from the tax component. For gasoline, note 76.82 cents per liter of mineral oil tax; for diesel 79.57. Remember that VAT is added to the amounts, while the 2025 revenue from the tax alone reached 4.367 billion.
This scheme does not anticipate a decision by the State and does not replace the reading of statistics. It serves to understand where high energy prices enter concrete life and why the national average does not always coincide with the bill of a family or a business. If the pressure remains, the data to be observed is the distance between expenses and income, not just the percentage of the index.
Detecting this distance helps not to confuse the tax data with the overall effect on the budget: the tax is a component, the cascading effect affects several items. To compare income with expenses, open the calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Swiss cost of living 2026: Canton of Bern in comparison
item.description: Rents, taxation, KVG and contributions: 2026 guide to the cost of living in the canton of Bern, with rules and comparisons valid in Switzerland.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - In 2026, the Swiss budget has three tax levels - In Bern, the KVG varies by canton and region - KVG coverage must be taken out within three months - The rental deposit is a maximum of three rents
## Key Facts - Taxation → federal IFD, cantonal and municipal taxes - Deductibles for adults → CHF 300/500/1000/1500/2000/2500 - Lease → maximum deposit of three months' rent - Contributions → AHV/IV/EO: 5.3% payable by the employee - Working → maximum hours of 45 or 50 hours per week
In 2026, the cost of living in Switzerland can be read through rents, food spending, transport and insurance. The canton of Bern is the point of observation of the analysis, but the comparison must distinguish what is valid throughout the country from what changes between cantons, regions and municipalities. To build an orderly picture, we can start from costo della vita in Svizzera, separating the items of expenditure from the rules that determine disposable income.
### The rules that make the difference
Taxation has three levels: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each canton has its own law and multiplier; the municipality applies a multiplier to the cantonal tax. For the canton of Bern, therefore, the budget reading is not limited to gross income: the municipal level is included in the overall calculation. The FTA/ESTV is responsible for direct federal tax and VAT, while the cantonal administrations follow the cantonal and municipal taxes. The FSIO/BSV, on the other hand, concerns social security, including AHV/AHV, IV and BVG/BVG, and does not set tax rates. The FSO/BFS produces statistics and does not set taxes.
The KVG is compulsory for residents and must be taken out within three months of arrival. It is a private insurance with per capita premiums, not a tax or a wage contribution. Premiums vary by canton and region; the premium reduction is a cantonal subsidy. For adults, the deductibles available are CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000 and 2500.
Tenancy also has a uniform federal framework. The CO, Art. 253 et seq., limits the security deposit to three months' rent and imposes an escrow account in the name of the tenant. The landlord's termination is only valid on the official cantonal form; the objection must be submitted to the conciliation authority within 30 days.
This distinction makes it possible to read the canton of Bern without confusing private expenditure, such as the KVG premium, with a deduction from wages or a tax. The same grid is applicable to the national comparison: the cantonal and municipal variables change, while the federal rules remain the common reference. ## From gross salary to real budget
Comparing the cost of living in the canton of Bern cannot stop at rent. Disposable income depends on the separation of social deductions, pensions, health insurance and taxes. To compare cantons, we start with the basis for each item.
### Deductions to be read in the payslip
For the employee, AHV/IV/EO is 5.3%; the total with the employer reaches 10.6%. AD/AC is 1.1% up to the annual ceiling. LAA/LAA ranges between 0.7% and 1.5% depending on the sector. The BVG/BVG on the coordinated salary provides for 7% between 25 and 34 years old, 10% between 35 and 44, 15% between 45 and 54, 18% from 55 years old up to the reference age.
| Voice | Rule to check | | AHV/IV/EO | 5.3% employee; 10.6% total with employer | | AD/AC | 1.1% up to the annual ceiling | | UVG/LAA | 0.7%-1.5% depending on the sector | | BVG/BVG | 7%, 10%, 15% or 18% by age group |
This separation avoids treating each percentage as if it had the same basis. The BVG concerns the coordinated salary; the AD is subject to an annual ceiling. For a more orderly reading of the salary, the comparison with AVS/LPP/rendita can be added.
The KVG premium remains a separate item from salary: it is per capita, not a tax or a wage contribution. For adults, the deductible can be CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000 or 2500, while premiums and reductions depend on the canton or region. The comparison can be deepened with LAMal/cassa malati.
Work also changes the reading of the budget. There is no federal minimum wage, although some cantons have their own. The maximum working time is 45 hours per week in industry, offices and sales, or 50 in other sectors. The minimum holidays are four weeks, five for those under 20 years of age; maternity leave lasts 14 weeks at 80% through EO and paternity leave two weeks. The notice periods are one, two or three months respectively in the first year, from the second to the ninth and from the tenth year.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## Practical procedure for 2026
### Five checks before comparison
1. Start with your living location. If you are a resident, the KVG is mandatory and must be concluded within three months of arrival. Compare the canton and region premium and check the cantonal reduction. For adults, note the deductible between CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000 and 2500.
2. Read the payslip for separate items. Consider AHV/IV/EO, ALV/CA, UVG/LAA and BVP/BVG: the ALV has an annual ceiling, the UVG depends on the sector and the BVG on the coordinated salary and age. Learn more with busta paga svizzera.
3. Separate taxes. FTA/ESTV covers IFD and VAT; cantonal administrations follow cantonal and municipal taxes. In Bern, it takes into account the municipal multiplier. FSO/BFS makes statistics, FSIO/BSV is about pensions: neither sets rates. Use the dichiarazione delle imposte guide.
4. Check the tenancy agreement. The CO, Art. 253 et seq., applies uniformly in the cantons: the deposit does not exceed three months' rent and remains in an escrow account in the name of the tenant. If you receive a notice of termination from the landlord, check the official cantonal form; you have 30 days to dispute it before the conciliation authority.
5. Classify work and leave. There is no federal minimum wage, while some cantons have their own. The maximum working time is 45 hours in industry, offices and sales, or 50 in other sectors. The SEM distinguishes between L up to one year, B renewable, C usually after 10 years of residence or 5 for EU/EFTA and G for cross-border commuters. The minimum leave is four weeks, five under 20 years; maternity leave 14 weeks at 80%, paternity leave two weeks and termination of 1, 2 or 3 months depending on seniority.
To turn the comparison into a personal estimate, use the calcolatore stipendio/imposte.

item.title: Council of States: yes to EU health agreement
item.description: 31 yes, 11 no: health decree approved. Optional referendum chosen. Electricity paused.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Council of States: yes to the agreement on health - Health: 31 votes in favour, 11 against, 1 abstention - Health referendum: optional one chosen - Electricity: exam objective in the winter session
## Key Facts - EU package → all approved decrees, except the electricity agreement - Resolutions → a total of 24 hours - Agreement on health → 31 in favor, 11 against, 1 abstention - Referendum on health → optional; 30 in favour, 12 against, 2 abstentions - Food security → 28 in favour, 14 against, 2 abstentions - Electricity agreement → the work of the committee not completed - Erasmus+ credit → 192.6 million from 2027
### The vote on health
By 31 votes to 11 with one abstention, the Council of States today approved the new agreement on health and thus completed the examination of the federal decrees of the package of agreements with the EU, with the sole exception of the agreement on electricity, which is not yet ready to be dealt with. After a total of 24 hours of deliberations, the health dossier now goes to the National Council.
The health agreement is part of further developments in relations with the EU. It provides for closer cooperation between Bern and Brussels on health security, with the aim indicated by Elisabeth Baume-Schneider of better protecting the population during crises. The health minister recalled the experience of the pandemic: "Covid-19 has clearly shown that a pandemic does not stop at borders."
The new agreement allows direct, complete and permanent access to the EU's health security mechanisms and the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control. It also strengthens the ability to anticipate, prepare for and react to the spread of new virus variants. Flavia Wasserfallen (SP/BE), on behalf of the committee, stressed that the country fully retains its sovereignty when adopting health measures. The possibility of extending cooperation to other areas of health is envisaged, provided that it is in the interest of both parties. In the EU's multiannual programme, Switzerland will only participate in the area of crisis preparedness. This topic can be combined with information on LAMal/cassa malati, while keeping the parliamentary level separate from the information level.
The People's Party, supported by some elected representatives of the Centre and the FDP, was against the agreement. Esther Friedli objected to the presence of institutional elements in a treaty that, in her opinion, should be one of cooperation and not of access to the internal market. The proposal to submit the agreement to a mandatory referendum did not pass: with 30 votes to 12 with 2 abstentions, the optional referendum was preferred.
Like the stabilisation of the package and the agreement on food security, which was approved by 28 votes to 14 with 2 abstentions, the health dossier will therefore have to be examined by the National Council. In order to enter into force, the stabilisation section will have to enter into force as a whole. According to the Council of States, a yes vote from both chambers and a mandatory popular vote with a double majority of the people and cantons will also be required. At the end of the Bilateral III, Stefan Engler thanked the Federal Council, the committees and the parliamentary services for the marathon debate. ## Dossiers do not have the same calendar
The vote of the states does not close the entire package. The distinction counts in understanding when a parliamentary decision can enter into force: in the case of the electricity agreement, the procedure has not yet reached the examination of the Chamber of Cantons; in the other dossiers, the next step is the National Council and, for stabilization, the condition of the overall entry into force remains.
### Electricity remains open
The competent committee has not concluded its work. Thierry Burkart has indicated the winter session as his objective, after more than twenty hours dedicated to the dossier and the hearing of numerous experts. The discussion does not concern an isolated technical detail: the disputed points are the complete opening of the market required by the agreement and the fear of a transfer of Swiss sovereignty over energy resources, in particular hydropower. The commission is also looking for a solution to maintain the minimum price of solar electricity fed into the grid by small plants.
These elements explain why the electricity agreement follows a different path from the acts already adopted. There is still no decision by the States on that text; the announced goal is to discuss it later. For those who follow the costo della vita in Svizzera, the point to be recorded is procedural: the examination remains open.
### Erasmus+ and stabilisation
On the stabilisation front, the states approved the commitment credit of CHF 192.6 million for Switzerland's participation in Erasmus+ from 2027, by 23 votes to 19 with 2 abstentions. The vote shows that the dossier remains politically disputed. The SECC-S had called for the relevant decree to be approved by a narrow majority, while Guy Parmelin argued that the benefits clearly outweigh the costs. He also warned that a parliamentary refusal could be received negatively by the EU in the overall assessment of the discussions.
For the reader, the practical consequence is a multi-level sequence: an approved credit alone does not equate to the entry into force of the entire stabilization; the package remains linked to the outcome of the other parliamentary passages and the popular vote indicated by the Council of States. The game on health, food safety and electricity therefore do not have the same calendar.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to follow the next steps
For those who want to know when a decision of the Council of States becomes operational, it is advisable to follow a precise sequence. The EU package should be read as a series of dossiers, not as a single vote.
### Four practical controls
1. National Council. To verify the passage of the health agreement, the stabilisation section and the food safety agreement. These are the dossiers that the Council of States has submitted to the National Council for scrutiny.
2. Applicable referendum. For health, the optional referendum has been chosen. For the entry into force linked to stabilisation, the Council of States instead indicates a mandatory popular vote with a double majority of the people and cantons. Do not confuse the two paths.
3. Overall condition. The health agreement will only be able to enter into force if the stabilization comes into force as a whole. Therefore, the mere vote in favor of a single decree does not close the procedure.
4. Winter session. For the electricity agreement, check the outcome of the work of the CAPTE-S and any examination in the winter session. Until then, the issues indicated by the commission remain open: complete opening of the market, sovereignty over energy resources and minimum price for solar for small plants.
A separate check concerns Erasmus+. The approved commitment credit concerns participation from 2027 and should be read within the stabilisation part, not as a conclusion of the whole package. Guy Parmelin's statements on the benefit-cost ratio and the possible negative judgment of the EU in the event of rejection explain why the credit has been carefully monitored, but do not replace institutional steps.
To organize the reading, three items can be noted for each dossier: competent chamber, type of referendum and condition for entry into force. It is the easiest way not to confuse the health agreement, already voted but not yet final, with the electricity agreement, still to be examined. To assess the effect of the decisions on your budget, use the calcolatore stipendio.

## In brief - September 30, 2026: Dismantled the network used by KillSec - Three arrests and eight searches in four countries - Recovered at least 110 terabytes of stolen data - OAG and fedpol involved as operational and strategic partners
## Key Facts - Published → 1 October 2026 - Criminal proceedings → from 31 July 2025 - Transaction → 30 September 2026 - International coordination → Europol and Eurojust with 7 other countries - Arrests → three individuals - Searches → eight, in Spain, Greece, the United Kingdom and Romania - Data recovered → at least 110 terabytes - Servers seized → five
On 30 September 2026, a large-scale international operation led to the dismantling of an IT structure used by the ransomware group "KillSec". The Federal Office of Police fedpol and the Office of the Attorney General of Switzerland (OAG) were directly involved as operational and strategic partners. The communiqué was published on 1 October 2026.
The intervention led to the arrest of three individuals and the seizure of evidence and assets. Eight searches were carried out in Spain, Greece, the United Kingdom and Romania. The authorities recovered at least 110 terabytes of stolen data and seized five servers that the group used to store its victims' data. The seizure therefore concerned both the storage infrastructure and other evidence.
### The Swiss file
Since 31 July 2025, the OAG has been conducting criminal proceedings against unknown persons for data theft, abusive access to a computer system, data damage and extortion. The press release also includes references to Articles 143, 143bis, 144bis and 156 of the SCC. The file was created after a series of ransomware attacks against various Swiss companies, attributed to KillSec, or "KillSecurity", between October 2023 and June 2025.
The investigations were conducted internationally and coordinated by Europol and Eurojust together with 7 other countries. fedpol and the OAG participated in the activities, while the dismantling operation took place on 30 September 2026.
### The double extortion method
The source also reconstructs how ransomware works. The perpetrators improperly access the victim's system, copy and extract the data of interest, then encrypt the servers and demand a ransom in exchange for the decryption key. Payment is often demanded in cryptocurrency.
KillSec practices so-called "double extortion": after the encryption of the servers, if the company refuses to pay, the perpetrators threaten to publish the data on the darknet. The source cites the existence of a backup made before the data was stolen as a possible reason for the refusal. ## What it means for those who do business in Switzerland
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the most concrete operational point is the audience of possible targets. The OFCS specifies that anyone can be one: a public body, a company or a private individual. Not only companies of strategic importance, therefore. The report is not presented as a step reserved for large groups, but as a tool to strengthen investigations and the fight against cybercrime.
### Two risks in the same attack
The dynamics described in the press release combine operational blocking and data exposure. The encryption of the servers creates the ransom demand to obtain the key; the copying and extraction of the data, on the other hand, opens up the threat of publication on the darknet. Even those who can refuse payment, for example because they have a backup prior to the theft, are therefore exposed to the second pressure. The text describes this mechanism and the investigative response of the authorities.
The reference to cryptocurrency also delimits the nature of the request: the ransom is linked to the decryption key. The issue remains distinct from the information on conti bancari in Svizzera: here the point is the theft, encryption and possible disclosure of data.
### Before and after the seizure
Before the operation, the IT structure allowed the group to store victims' data on its servers. After the seizure, the authorities explain that disrupting the operation of the network and stealing servers and data limits the ability of the perpetrators to continue criminal activities. The seized material also serves to collect new evidence, to support the identification of cybercriminals and to better understand the role and degree of involvement of the different actors.
However, the coup does not close the proceedings. The investigations by the OAG and fedpol are continuing. The presumption of innocence applies to all participants and the OAG does not provide any further information on the ongoing investigation. For the productive fabric, the only verifiable conclusion is therefore twofold: cooperation can disrupt an infrastructure, but the criminal investigation continues according to the ongoing proceedings.
### A response that passes through the cantons
The preparatory work was carried out by fedpol under the direction of the OAG, in collaboration with the cantonal police and the OFCS. The investigators collected and analysed detailed information on the network's modus operandi and coordinated exchanges with foreign partners. The resources on aziende che assumono relate to the labour market; this case, on the other hand, shows how a digital threat can involve companies and authorities on several levels.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## What to do after an attack
The OFCS warning indicates a clear course of action for those who suffer a cyber attack in Switzerland: report the facts to the competent authorities or file a complaint directly with the police or the OAG. The path applies to a public body, a company and a private individual, because the source considers each person to be a potential target.
### Four steps indicated by the source
1. Recognize the case. The ransomware described involves undue access to the system, copying and extracting data, encrypting servers and demanding a ransom, often in cryptocurrency. The so-called double extortion adds the threat of publishing data on the darknet when the victim does not pay.
2. Select the channel. The report can be addressed to the competent authorities. Alternatively, the report can be submitted directly to the police or the Office of the Attorney General of Switzerland. The OFCS calls out both possibilities and links the report to strengthening the investigation.
3. Activate cooperation. The facts reported contribute to the investigative work carried out by fedpol under the direction of the OAG, together with the cantonal police and the OFCS. The information collected can feed into exchanges with foreign partners, a component already used in the investigations into the group.
4. Consider judicial follow-up. The authorities continue to identify the perpetrators, arrest them and, when they are abroad and circumstances permit, request extradition to Switzerland. The stated objective is also to obtain a criminal conviction.
### After reporting
The recall of the OFCS is not limited to companies of strategic importance. It includes public bodies, companies and individuals, i.e. all those who the source considers potential targets. The report serves to strengthen investigations and, more generally, to combat cybercrime.
The statement states that the presumption of innocence applies to all participants and that the OAG will not provide any further information on the ongoing criminal investigation for the time being. However, the activities of the OAG and fedpol continue. For those operating in Switzerland, the choice indicated by the OFCS remains concrete: report the attack to the competent authorities or file a complaint with the police or the OAG.

item.title: Oversharing and AI at work: Cyber Security Month 2026 guide
item.description: On 1 October 2026, the FOCS will launch Cyber Security Month in Bern on the topic of "Oversharing – sharing with awareness", together with Netpathie and the FDPIC.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The FOCS dedicates October 2026 to "oversharing" - Photos, numbers, and names together outline profiles - The FOCS will discuss the topic over the next four weeks - Focus also on AI in working life
## Key Facts - Date → 1 October 2026 - Location → Bern - Theme → "Oversharing – sharing with awareness" - Illustrated period → next four weeks - Collaboration → Netpathie
On 1 October 2026, the Federal Office for Cybersecurity (FOCS) dedicated Cyber Security Month in Bern to the topic "Oversharing – sharing with awareness". The message concerns habits in social media, everyday working life and the use of artificial intelligence: every day we share information and leave digital traces, often more than we realize.
A photo, phone number, or name may appear harmless individually. When combined, however, they can build a surprisingly detailed picture of a person. According to the FOCS, information published on the Internet can become valuable to criminals. Possible uses include personalized phishing, identity theft, fraud, and targeted manipulation.
Over the next four weeks, the FOCS will explain where oversharing begins, what risks it entails and how to handle information more consciously. The October campaign was carried out, as it was last year, in collaboration with Netpathie.
### Workshop between generations
The programme includes intergenerational workshops. Young people and older adults address the topic together on the basis of concrete examples. The aim of the workshops is to show how quickly individual pieces of information can form a personal profile and how this profile can be used for criminal purposes. Participants also develop strategies for sharing data more consciously and for recognising suspicious situations at an early stage.
### Work enters the countryside
In 2026, the focus will be on artificial intelligence in everyday work. Artificial intelligence offers numerous possibilities, for example for drafting emails, translating texts or analyzing data. At the same time, new risks arise when personal, confidential or company information is recklessly entered into AI tools.
In cooperation with the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC), the FOCS sheds light on the use of AI in everyday working life and the associated cybersecurity risks. At the heart of the campaign is a question: what information can be entrusted to an AI tool and what is better not to provide? ## What changes in practice
The practical value of the campaign lies in changing the moment in which information is evaluated: not only after publication, but before bringing together details that, taken separately, seem harmless. The decisive element described by the FOCS is the combination: the personal picture becomes more detailed when the information is linked.
The same logic is transferred to everyday work. Writing an email, translating a text and analyzing data are activities cited by the FOCS as possibilities of artificial intelligence. The delicate step comes when personal, confidential or business information is entered into an AI tool to carry them out. The question is not whether AI is useful: the question indicated by the campaign is what information can be entrusted to the tool and what is better not to provide.
For an employee, the distinction leads to a concrete verification. Before sharing content, it is necessary to recognize what kind of information it contains; then to ask oneself whether it is really necessary to include it in the tool; and finally to stop when the content is personal, confidential or corporate and it is not clear whether it can be entrusted. This is an operational reading of the question posed by the FOCS and FDPIC, not a new technical regulation indicated in the press release.
### A theme that crosses generations
The workshops aimed at young people and older adults show that the issue is not confined to just one age group or channel. Social media, work life and AI belong to different situations, but they share the same risk described by the FOCS: leaving more information than is intended.
The collaboration with Netpathie adds a direct comparison. Through concrete examples, participants can see how quickly a personal profile is built and work on more conscious sharing strategies. For those who want to keep information security distinct from the economic tools of working life, the site also offers busta paga svizzera and calcolatore stipendio. Here, however, the point remains the choice of content to share.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## A procedure before sharing
To turn the UFCS’s message into a daily practice, the check must be carried out before sharing. The point is not to wait until a piece of data seems dangerous: it is necessary to observe how several details can be linked.
1. Identify the content. Ask yourself whether you are sharing a photo, a phone number, a name or a set of information. The source shows that these elements, when combined, can outline a personal profile. 2. Look at the context. Assess the whole, not just the individual piece of data: this is where the shift toward oversharing can be recognized. 3. Classify the information. If its use concerns working life and an AI tool, check whether the content is personal, confidential or corporate. 4. Ask the decisive question. Before using AI to draft an email, translate a text or analyze data, ask yourself which information you can entrust to it and which is better not to provide. 5. Recognize the signs. Apply the strategies developed to promptly identify suspicious situations, both when you post on the Internet and when you use AI.
### Following Cybersecurity Month
Over the next four weeks, the UFCS will explain where oversharing begins, the risks and ways to manage information with greater awareness. This schedule makes it possible to observe one’s own digital habits without confusing a single piece of information with the profile that may emerge from their combination.
A second step consists in observing the concrete examples used in intergenerational workshops: the campaign uses them to show young people and older adults how a personal profile is formed and to develop shared strategies. The criterion remains the one indicated by the UFCS together with the IFPDT: first assess which information to entrust to an AI tool.

item.title: Council of States approves EU healthcare agreement
item.description: 31 against 11: green light for EU healthcare. Now to the National. Optional referendum chosen, electricity in winter.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Council of States approves health agreement - The dossier now goes to the National Council - The chosen referendum is the optional one - Electricity remains to be examined
## Key Facts - Agreement on health → 31 votes to 11, 1 abstention - Resolutions → a total of 24 hours - EU access → direct, complete and permanent - EU multiannual programme → crisis preparedness only - Food security → 28 votes to 14, 2 abstentions - Electricity → exam objective in the winter session
### The vote and the content of the agreement
By 31 votes to 11 with one abstention, the Council of States today approved the new health agreement with the European Union. The dossier now goes to the National Council. With the exception of the electricity agreement, the Chamber of Cantons has thus completed its examination of the federal decrees of the EU package.
The deliberations lasted a total of 24 hours and took centre stage in the last week of the session. The health agreement is part of further developments in relations with Brussels and aims for closer cooperation on health security. For Elisabeth Baume-Schneider, the result serves to better protect the population in health crises.
"Covid-19 has clearly shown that a pandemic does not stop at borders," said the Federal Councillor. Switzerland's geographical location, according to Baume-Schneider, makes it necessary to have close exchanges with the European authorities. The agreement provides for direct, complete and permanent access to the EU's health security mechanisms and the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control.
The text also strengthens the ability to anticipate, prepare for and react to the spread of new virus variants. However, Switzerland retains its sovereignty in the adoption of health measures, Flavia Wasserfallen stressed on behalf of the committee. The agreement focuses on health security, but allows for a possible extension to other areas of health if it is in the interest of both parties. In the EU's multiannual programme, Switzerland's participation would only cover crisis preparedness.
The People's Party, supported by representatives of the Centre and the FDP, opposed it. Esther Friedli challenged the institutional elements of the agreement and the hypothesis of Brussels rules applicable in a future pandemic, recalling Switzerland's collaboration with the WHO. The attempt to impose the mandatory referendum was rejected: 30 votes to 12 and 2 abstentions confirmed the optional referendum. For a separate in-depth analysis of the LAMal e la cassa malati, the reader will find a dedicated tool. ## The Path That Remains Open
### Three Conditions for Entry into Force
The decision of the Council of States does not yet amount to the application of the agreement. For those who live or work in Switzerland, the practical point is that the dossier goes to the National Council and that entry into force is linked to the stabilization part of the package. The latter must enter into force as a whole. The timetable therefore depends on the parliamentary steps and the popular vote indicated by the Chamber of Cantons.
| Step | What it entails | |---|---| | National Council | New examination of the dossier | | Stabilization | Entry into force as a whole | | People and Cantons | Mandatory vote with a double majority |
The most delicate point is the relationship between the referendum chosen for the health agreement and the condition envisaged for stabilization. The Council of States opted for the optional referendum for the health agreement, with 30 votes to 12 and 2 abstentions. In the same context, however, the Chamber of Cantons considers a mandatory popular vote with the double majority of the People and the Cantons necessary, in addition to approval by both chambers, for the stabilization part to enter into force. The practical reading is that the individual vote on healthcare does not by itself settle the entire dossier.
In terms of substance, the announced scope is limited: health security, access to European mechanisms and Swiss participation only in the crisis-preparedness sector of the EU multiannual programme. Any possible extension to other areas of health is subject to the interest of both parties. Switzerland also retains the authority to adopt its own health measures. These are the points to assess when the text goes before the National Council, without conflating cooperation with access to the internal market, a distinction raised by Esther Friedli.
The rest of the package also has different timelines. The agreement on food security was adopted by the Council of States with 28 votes to 14 and 2 abstentions, but still has to be examined by the National Council. The electricity agreement, by contrast, was not taken up in the sitting because the competent committee has not completed its work; the announced target is the winter session. Anyone seeking a broader overview of costo della vita in Svizzera must therefore keep that topic separate from the procedure described here.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to follow the process without confusing the steps
### A checklist in four steps
1. Start with the parliamentary state. The agreement on health has been approved by the Council of States, but the dossier is now destined for the National Council. The first test therefore consists in seeking the outcome of the examination of the second chamber, not in interpreting the vote of the states as a conclusion.
2. Separate the three dossiers. Health and food safety follow the next step towards the National Council; electricity follows a separate timetable, with the goal of the winter session announced by the competent committee. This separation avoids considering the entire EU package already completed.
3. Check the stabilisation clause. The health agreement can only enter into force if the stabilisation part enters into force as a whole. The review must therefore cover the complete package, not just the outcome on the health chapter.
4. Check the popular requirement. According to the Council of States, a yes vote from both chambers and a mandatory popular vote with a double majority of the people and cantons are needed. The optional referendum chosen for the health agreement should be read next to this overall condition, not in its place.
### What to read in the final text
When the dossier advances, there are five substantial points to be monitored: direct, complete and permanent access to EU health security mechanisms; liaison with the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control; the possibility of anticipating, preparing for and reacting to new virus variants; the continuation of Swiss sovereignty over health measures; participation only in the area of crisis preparedness in the EU multiannual programme. Whether it should be extended to other areas of health depends on the interests of both parties.
For readers residing in the cantons, this grid makes it possible to distinguish what has been voted on from what still needs to go through the National Council and, depending on the position of the states, through the people and the cantons. There is no need to attribute effects to the agreement that the source does not describe: its declared perimeter concerns health security and cooperation with Brussels.
